record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.original_question: Consider smooth maps u: R^2 -> R^2 solving the entire Ginzburg-Landau equation Delta u = u(1 - |u|^2) on R^2 and satisfying |u(x)| -> 1 as |x| -> infinity, so that the degree at infinity deg(u,infinity) is defined. For each integer q, the source defines a distinguished vortex V_q(r,theta)=exp(i q theta) g_q(r), with V_0 identically 1. Must every solution u coincide with V_q, up to multiplication by a unit complex number and translation in R^2, where q = deg(u,infinity)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.4 ([3, Problem 14], [13, 25]). Let u be any solution of (2.4)-(2.5). Does u coincide with V_q modulo rotation and translation, where q = deg(u,infinity)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider smooth maps $u:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$, identified with $\mathbb{C}$, that solve the entire Ginzburg–Landau equation
$$\Delta u = u\,(|u|^2-1) \quad \text{on } \mathbb{R}^2,$$
and satisfy $|u(x)|\to 1$ as $|x|\to\infty$. Under this asymptotic condition, the map $u/|u|$ is well-defined for $|x|$ large and has a well-defined topological degree $\deg(u,\infty)\in\mathbb{Z}$ as a map from a large circle to $S^1$. For each integer $q$, let
$$V_q(r,\theta) := e^{i q\theta}\,g_q(r),$$
where $(r,\theta)$ are polar coordinates on $\mathbb{R}^2$, with $V_0\equiv 1$, and where for $q\ne 0$, $g_q:[0,\infty)\to[0,1)$ is the unique solution of the ODE
$$g_q''(r)+\frac{1}{r}g_q'(r)-\frac{q^2}{r^2}g_q(r)+g_q(r)(1-g_q(r)^2)=0,\qquad g_q(0)=0,\ \lim_{r\to\infty}g_q(r)=1,$$
which gives the equivariant vortex of degree $q$.

Determine whether every such solution $u$ must coincide with $V_q$ up to multiplication by a unit complex number and translation of $\mathbb{R}^2$, where $q=\deg(u,\infty)$. That is, must there exist $\alpha\in S^1\subset\mathbb{C}$ and $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^2$ such that
$$u(x)=\alpha\,V_q(x-x_0)\qquad \text{for all } x\in\mathbb{R}^2\ ?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of entire Ginzburg-Landau vortices in the plane is widely cited as an open problem. Partial results exist: for degree $|q|=1$, Mironescu and others established uniqueness/stability properties; in higher dimensions $N\ge 7$, uniqueness of the degree-one equivariant vortex as a minimizer in the unit ball was proved by Ignat–Nguyen–Slastikov–Zarnescu. However, the full classification in $\mathbb{R}^2$ for all degrees $q$ remains unresolved in the recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of degree-one Ginzburg–Landau vortex in the unit ball in dimensions N ≥ 7
status_evidence.snippet: For every ε>0 there exists a unique global minimizer u_ε with vortex boundary data; u_ε is symmetric.
status_evidence.claim: Related uniqueness results known in high dimensions for the bounded-domain version, indicating the entire R^2 problem is a long-standing question.
